question.leadin: This country's emperor, Menelik II, stopped an Italian invasion of his country at the Battle of Adwa.
question.text: Along with Liberia, what nation in the Horn of Africa led from Addis Ababa is considered to be the only African nation not to be colonized?
question.clue: The Hayamots helped Gebre Lalibela's line defeat Queen Gudit, who had ended a golden age that saw this country defeat Dhu Nuwas and the Himyarites and take control of Yemen.

swap.text: Not to be accused of lacking attention to detail, Amin also clarified that he was the conqueror of this country "in Particular". Idi Amin brutally ruled this country for most of the 1970s, during which he expelled all Asians from it.
swap.clue: In 1972, the Jews and Asians were expelled from this country, in which several hostages were rescued in a raid on Entebbe.

question.leadin: Name these former British Colonies in Africa.
question.text: This country was subjected to British Control after the Battle of Omdurman in 1898. Its capital is Khartoum, and in 2011 its southern part became an independent nation with a similar name.
question.clue: General Marchand marched his forces to Fashoda in this country during one incident here.

swap.leadin: As a result of the Rivonia Trial, this man was imprisoned on Robben Island.
swap.text: Name this man who succeeded Frederik Willem de Klerk as president of South Africa.
swap.clue: He wrote the autobiography Long Walk to Freedom, and was held at Robben Island prison for many years.

question.leadin: This man founded the De Beers Company to take advantage of a diamond mining rush.
question.text: Name this British colonialist who was depicted as a giant towering over Africa in several cartoons. This man is the namesake of an international postgraduate scholarship to study at Oxford.
question.clue: Charles Rudd and this man convinced King Lobengula to hand over the resource-rich Matebeland; this was known as the "Rudd Concession."

swap.text: At the Battle of Tondibi, the Moroccan army defeated the forces of Askia Ishaq II, who in 1588 took power in this African empire, a center of Trans-Saharan trade.
swap.clue: Forces of this empire were lead by Ishaq II when it lost to Moroccan forces at Tondibi.

question.text: Prince Johnson suggested that this country's president Charles Taylor had ordered the overthrow of Sankara. Taylor himself came to power after overthrowing this country's leader Samuel Doe.
question.clue: The rigged 1985 election in this country was won by Samuel Doe, who was replaced by a man who gave Pat Robertson special mining rights in this country.

swap.leadin: Until photos of one leader's corpse appeared on TV and the US Department of Defense confirmed he was killed in battle, this country had trouble believing he was dead.
swap.text: Name this home country of Jonas Savimbi. The UNITA and MPLA fought a decades-long civil war in this country following its independence from Portugal.
swap.clue: The battles of Quifangondo ("ki-fun-gahn-dough") and Cuito Cuanavale were fought in this country's civil war.

question.leadin: The British defeated the forces of a sultanate on this archipelago in the shortest recorded war.
question.text: Name this archipelago which the Sultan of Oman seized in 1698. This archipelago later merged with Tanganyika.
question.clue: Like nearby Mafia Island and Pemba Island, this island is called a "spice island" for its production of cloves.

swap.text: One Door of No Return memorial is located in modern-day Benin, the site of this African kingdom. The Europeans who obtained slaves from the rulers of this kingdom referred to this kingdom's female warriors as "Amazons."
swap.clue: After destroying the Wemenou, this kingdom was harassed by the Oyo.

question.leadin: This kingdom collapsed after a defeat by the French at the Battle of Poguessa.
question.text: Name this African kingdom that ruled over the Fon people and was a leading supplier of slaves to European empires. It was located in present day Benin.
question.clue: The city of Allada, the home of this empire's founder Do-Aklin, was captured by its king Adaja.

swap.leadin: In 2003, this woman founded the Mazingira Green Party to promote her ecological platform.
swap.text: Name this Kenyan Woman who won the Nobel Peace Prize for her work as the founder of the Green Belt Movement.
swap.clue: This environmental, political, and social activist, who became the first African woman and the first environmentalist to win the Nobel Peace Prize.

question.leadin: To enforce a UN sanction on this man's country, the British Royal Navy instituted a largely unsuccessful blockade of the port of Beira.
question.text: Name this prime minister of Rhodesia who defended white minority rule until the signing of the Lancaster House Agreement in 1979.
question.clue: His tenure ended with the Internal Settlement, under which he was replaced by Bishop Abel Muzorewa, and soon after, he was definitively removed by the Lancaster House Conference.

swap.leadin: Subgroups of this ethnicity include the Chaoui, Shilha, and the Kabyle.
swap.text: Name this broad ethnic group indigenous to North Africa. Their name is derived from the Latin word "barbaros."
swap.clue: The Strait of Gibraltar is named for a military commander of this ethnic group.

question.leadin: This man was accused of directing the Mau Mau rebellion of 1952 and was sentenced to seven years in prison.
question.text: Name this first prime minister and president of independent Kenya.
question.clue: He also represented the Kikuyu tribe in testifying at the Carter Land Commission.

swap.leadin: Using a script developed by Shire Jama Ahmed, this dictator mandated literacy in his native language by all government officials.
swap.text: Identify this dictator who ruled from 1969 to 1991 and who outlawed the qabil system of clan affiliation, used the Red Berets and Victory Pioneers to terrorize his populace, and coveted Ogaden, Djibouti, and Northeastern Kenya.
swap.answerHtml: Mohamed Siad Barre [or Maxamed Siyaad Barre if you enjoy Somali script]
swap.clue: This "Scientific Socialism" proponent negotiated with Helmut Schmidt to let German special forces retrieve a PFLP-hijacked Lufthansa plane.

question.text: From 1958 until his death in 1984, Toure led this African nation on the Atlantic, which is bordered by Mali and the Ivory Coast, among others, as well as a similarly named former Portuguese colony.

swap.leadin: This man was a member of the Krahn tribe, and resentment toward Americo-Liberians fed his rise to power.
swap.text: Identify this dictator of Liberia from 1980-90 who established the People's Redemption Council. He was overthrown by rebels including Prince Johnson, who flmed his torture and may have eaten his ear.

question.text: The San were recruited as scouts and trackers [emphasize] against this cause, which was sought after by SWAPO.

swap.leadin: He signed the 1996 Abidjan Agreement with Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, which had little effect on the ongoing civil war.
swap.text: Name this leader of the Revolutionary United Front who was to be tried for war crimes committed during the Sierra Leone civil war before his 2003 death from a stroke.
